advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the allowed-expression branch so only known-safe generated sources (e.g. `random_password.*.result`) are exempt; flag other unquoted `value =` expressions on a SecureString secret.
evidence: scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py:123: `has_expr_value = bool(value_match and value_match.group(1) != '"')`
scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py:140: `if not (has_value_wo or has_expr_value or has_literal_value or has_insecure_value):`
docstring only justifies the exemption for `random_password.x.result`, but the code allows every non-quoted expression, e.g. `value = var.secret`, which persists to state identically to a literal
advisory.finding: The guard treats ANY unquoted `value = <expression>` on a SecureString as an allowed 'terraform-generated' value, but a real secret sourced from a variable/local (e.g. `value = var.gerrit_password` or `value = local.secret`) is also an unquoted expression and WOULD be persisted to state — yet draws no finding. The gate's negative result cannot distinguish 'genuinely generated (random_password)' from 'operator secret injected via a variable', so a future secret-in-state regression via a variable reference passes silently.
scenarios: A new SecureString secret declared as `value = var.some_secret` with no ignore_changes
A migration that swaps `value = "CHANGEME"` for `value = local.seeded_value`
advisory.suggested_fix: Match the RHS expression against an allowlist (e.g. `^(random_password|random_id|random_string)\.`) rather than treating every non-quoted `value =` as generated-and-safe.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_block_body` robust to braces inside HCL strings/heredocs/comments, or document the assumption that ssm parameter blocks never contain such braces.
evidence: scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py:92-97: depth is adjusted on every raw `{`/`}` char with no string/comment handling
A `description = "... { ..."` or heredoc inside the block would unbalance the depth counter
advisory.finding: `_block_body` counts `{`/`}` literally with no awareness of braces inside HCL string literals, heredocs, or comments; a parameter block containing a `{` or `}` in a string/comment (e.g. a description or a JSON policy string) would truncate or over-extend the extracted body, causing the scan of that resource to mis-classify or skip attributes.
scenarios: A future aws_ssm_parameter block whose description or a heredoc contains an unbalanced brace

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make check_ssm_secret_state.py emit a VIOLATION when a SecureString `aws_ssm_parameter` declares `insecure_value` (plaintext-in-state), rather than accepting it as a valid value source.
evidence: scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py:126 `has_insecure_value = bool(_INSECURE_VALUE_RE.search(body))`

scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py:140 `if not (has_value_wo or has_expr_value or has_literal_value or has_insecure_value):` — insecure_value satisfies the 'has a value source' test, suppressing even the 'no value source' finding, and no branch emits a VIOLATION for insecure_value on a SecureString
The emit branches (lines 132-141) flag literal `value`, `ignore_changes=[value]`, and value_wo pairing errors, but there is NO branch that flags `has_insecure_value` on a SecureString
docstring line 66-67 acknowledges `insecure_value` is 'the provider's third value source (never valid for SecureString)' — a plaintext-in-state path — yet the gate lets it through
advisory.finding: The new SSM-secret state guard treats `insecure_value` as an acceptable value source and never flags it, so a future `aws_ssm_parameter` of type SecureString declared with `insecure_value = "..."` would pass the gate while persisting a plaintext secret into terraform state — the exact exposure class (plaintext secret in state) the gate exists to prevent.
scenarios: A future terraform edit declares a SecureString secret with `insecure_value = "..."` (e.g. copy-paste from a non-secret param); `make lint` stays green while the plaintext secret is written to remote state.
A partial migration where an author uses insecure_value instead of value_wo silently regresses the ADR 0105 invariant.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an explicit violation branch: `if has_insecure_value: add('declares `insecure_value` (plaintext, persisted to state) on a SecureString')`, and remove `has_insecure_value` from the 'no value source' acceptance set on line 140.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Flag `insecure_value` on a `SecureString` `aws_ssm_parameter` as a violation in check_ssm_secret_state.py rather than accepting it as a valid value source.
evidence: scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py:126 `has_insecure_value = bool(_INSECURE_VALUE_RE.search(body))`
scripts/check_ssm_secret_state.py:140 `if not (has_value_wo or has_expr_value or has_literal_value or has_insecure_value):`
The comment at line 66 itself states insecure_value is `never valid for SecureString`, yet it is counted as a satisfying value source and never flagged as a violation for a SecureString block.
advisory.finding: The SSM-secret state guard treats `insecure_value` as an acceptable value source for a `SecureString` parameter, but `insecure_value` is only valid on `type="String"` params and would store the value in cleartext in state for a SecureString — so a SecureString written with `insecure_value` passes the gate while defeating its purpose.
scenarios: A future SecureString secret is written with `insecure_value = "..."`; the gate stays green because insecure_value counts as a value source, yet the value is a plaintext literal the provider persists to state.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an explicit violation branch: `if has_insecure_value: add("declares insecure_value on a SecureString (plaintext in state; invalid for SecureString)")`, and drop has_insecure_value from the no-value-source guard so it never counts as a satisfying source.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the deferred cutover runbook sequences apply -> re-seed -> verify within one window and that user_data fail-fast + rollback are sufficient given all 23 secrets reset at once.
evidence: infra/terraform/ssm.tf:104-105 `value_wo = "CHANGEME"` / `value_wo_version = 1`

docs/adr/0105-ssm-secrets-never-in-terraform-state.md: `on the first apply, value_wo_version transitions from absent to 1 (a change), so the provider sends value_wo = "CHANGEME" once and resets the live value to the placeholder`
The clobber is documented and deferred to operator task 097b-de23-bf12-4c38 with user_data.sh CHANGEME fail-fast as the safety net, so the risk is acknowledged rather than unhandled.
advisory.finding: The one-time migration `apply` transitions `value_wo_version` from absent to `1` for all 23 seeded secrets simultaneously, so the provider re-sends `value_wo="CHANGEME"` and resets every live secret (Gerrit admin password, opcert key, bot signing key, Anthropic key, SSH host keys, Jira token, MCP PATs) to the placeholder in a single apply — a large simultaneous blast radius that requires all of them to be re-seeded in the same maintenance window.
scenarios: The deferred operator cutover applies the migration; between the apply and re-seeding, every secret slot holds CHANGEME and any instance (re)boot fails fast on the placeholder.

dropped.finding: `_VALUE_RE.search(body)` inspects only the FIRST `value =` occurrence in a block. A block that declares `value_wo`/`value_wo_version` first and then also (erroneously) a quoted `value = "..."` later is classified by whichever `value =` the single search hits; a half-migrated block that keeps both write-only and a plaintext value could be misjudged depending on ordering.
